Publication-style four-panel 3D fish trajectory storyboard

Source: R/trajectory-storyboard3d.R
aqt_plot_trajectory_storyboard3d.Rd

Produces a static 2 x 2 axonometric projection of a single observed physical-XYZ fish track. Earlier contiguous movement is grey; two non-overlapping recent windows are light and dark blue. The same physical tank bounds and view are used for all four panels.

Usage

aqt_plot_trajectory_storyboard3d(
  tracks,
  times_s = NULL,
  session_id = NULL,
  camera_id = NULL,
  track_id = NULL,
  recent_s = 2,
  max_gap_s = Inf,
  max_age_s = 0.2,
  tank_limits = NULL
)

Arguments

tracks

Validated 3D aqt_tracks in physical tank units (cm or m).

times_s

Four strictly increasing timestamps. NULL uses four equally spaced times across the observed trajectory duration.

session_id, camera_id, track_id

Optional identifiers selecting one fish scope. Required if input contains multiple scopes.

recent_s

Width (seconds) of each of the two recency bands.

max_gap_s

Largest allowed consecutive observed sampling interval; Inf permits any gap without an explicit missing row.

max_age_s

Largest allowed age of the last observed position for showing the current fish head and reporting its latest speed.

tank_limits

Optional list(x=c(min,max),y=c(min,max),z=c(min,max)) in the same physical units as tracks. Without it, visible bounds are inferred from supplied observed XYZ, not independently measured.

Value

Invisibly, a four-row data frame with audited per-frame observed distance, latest valid speed, current-observation status, and counts. Draws a four-panel static figure on the active base graphics device.

Details

Segments spanning explicitly missing fish observations or a time gap larger than max_gap_s are not connected or counted in distance. No depth is inferred from 2D pixels. The distance is the sum of observed valid segments, NOT an estimate of unobserved travel. Speed is measured over the most recent valid observed segment, not a smoothed or instantaneous biological velocity. Supplied physical coordinates and any external calibration require separate validation.
